question: You receive an urgent email claiming to be from your corporate IT Helpdesk stating your account will be deleted in 2 hours unless you confirm your password at 'helpdesk-update.example.net'. What is the most secure response?
options: Click the link immediately and submit your credentials to avoid disruption
Reply directly to the email asking if the message is legitimate
Report the email using the official phishing report button and verify with IT out-of-band
Forward the email to all your coworkers to warn them
explanation: High-urgency language coupled with an external domain link is a hallmark phishing tactic. Always use official reporting tools and verify via trusted internal channels.

question: When inspecting an email link, why is hovering your cursor over the hyperlink critical?
options: It automatically scans the destination server for malware
It reveals the true underlying destination URL, which may differ from the visible display text
It encrypts your local browser session before connection
It disables any tracking cookies embedded by the sender
explanation: Attackers frequently display benign-looking text (e.g. 'https://company.com') while linking to an external malicious or spoofed site. Hovering reveals the actual destination.

question: You receive a QR code in an email asking you to scan it with your personal smartphone to complete a mandatory 2FA update. What type of attack is this?
options: Quishing (QR Code Phishing)
Vishing (Voice Phishing)
DNS Cache Poisoning
Smishing (SMS Phishing)
explanation: Quishing uses QR codes to redirect victims from secure corporate workstations to unmonitored mobile browsers where credential harvesting pages can bypass desktop email filters.

question: Which of the following represents the strongest password practice according to modern defensive guidelines?
options: A 6-character password changed every 14 days
A 16+ character passphrase made of 4+ random unrelated words stored in a password manager
Your company name followed by your birth year and an exclamation mark
Sharing a single complex password across your personal and work accounts
explanation: Length and uniqueness provide maximum entropy against modern cracking algorithms. Passphrases stored in a password manager eliminate reuse vulnerabilities.

question: Why is reusing the exact same password across multiple online accounts considered a critical risk?
options: It slows down computer processor performance
If a single third-party site suffers a breach, attackers can use credential stuffing to access all your other accounts
Password managers refuse to save duplicate passwords
It violates standard HTTP protocol specifications
explanation: Credential stuffing automated tools test leaked username/password combos across thousands of banking, corporate, and cloud services simultaneously.

question: Where is the safest place to store complex, unique passwords for dozens of business accounts?
options: In a plain text file on your desktop titled 'passwords.txt'
In an enterprise-approved, encrypted Password Manager protected by strong MFA
Written on a sticky note attached under your keyboard
In a shared unencrypted spreadsheet on a public cloud drive
explanation: Encrypted password managers utilize AES-256 or zero-knowledge architecture, ensuring credentials cannot be read without master credentials and MFA.

question: You suddenly receive 15 consecutive MFA push notifications on your phone within two minutes without initiating a login. What attack are you experiencing?
options: Buffer Overflow
MFA Fatigue (Push Spamming) Attack
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
SQL Injection
explanation: Adversaries with compromised passwords bombard the user with push prompts hoping the user will click 'Approve' out of frustration or mistake.

question: Which multi-factor authentication method provides the highest resistance against Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing attacks?
options: SMS text verification codes
Email verification codes
FIDO2 / WebAuthn Hardware Security Keys (or Passkeys)
Answering secret security questions
explanation: FIDO2/WebAuthn binds authentication cryptographically to the exact origin domain, preventing reverse-proxy phishing kits from capturing session tokens.

question: A supposed colleague calls you asking for the 6-digit one-time code sent to your mobile phone so they can finish setting up your project access. What should you do?
options: Read them the code quickly so work is not delayed
Never share one-time authentication codes with anyone, as legitimate support will never ask for them
Text them the code along with your username
Ask them to call back in 5 minutes before reading it
explanation: One-time passcodes are strictly confidential verification credentials. IT staff and colleagues never have legitimate technical need to know your temporary MFA token.

question: An unknown caller claiming to be the CEO's executive assistant demands an immediate wire transfer to a new vendor, insisting standard procurement steps be skipped. What principle is the attacker exploiting?
options: Perceived Authority, Intimidation, and Manufactured Urgency
Technical protocol vulnerabilities in TCP/IP
Hardware memory corruption
Network routing misconfiguration
explanation: Business Email Compromise (BEC) and executive vishing rely heavily on psychological pressure, urgency, and perceived organizational hierarchy to bypass controls.

question: What is the cybersecurity term for an attacker attempting to follow closely behind an authorized employee through a badge-secured security door?
options: Phreaking
Tailgating / Piggybacking
War-driving
Brute-forcing
explanation: Tailgating is a physical social engineering vulnerability where an unauthorized person gains physical building entry by following an authorized individual.

question: You receive a phone call from someone claiming to be Microsoft Windows Tech Support claiming your machine has viruses and requesting remote desktop access. What is the correct action?
options: Allow remote access immediately so they can clean your system
Provide credit card info to buy the recommended antivirus subscription
Hang up immediately; major tech vendors never initiate unsolicited cold calls about computer health
Leave the computer on and walk away
explanation: Unsolicited tech support calls are classic vishing scams designed to install remote access trojans (RATs) and extort payments.

question: Your browser displays a red warning screen: 'Your connection is not private - Potential security risk ahead.' What is the safest course of action?
options: Click advanced and proceed anyway to see the content
Do NOT proceed or submit sensitive data; inspect whether the domain or network is compromised
Disable your antivirus firewall and refresh the page
Switch to incognito mode and enter your credit card
explanation: SSL/TLS certificate mismatches can indicate expired certificates or an active adversary intercepting traffic on the local network.

question: What is 'Typosquatting' (URL Hijacking)?
options: A fast typing contest held in security conventions
Registering domain names that look almost identical to popular sites (e.g., 'examp1e.com') to catch mistyped URLs
A hardware keyboard logging device
An automated text compression technique
explanation: Typosquatting relies on user typographical errors to lure victims to clone sites hosting malware or credential harvesters.

question: Why should you regularly audit and remove unused browser extensions?
options: Extensions can consume storage and can be updated by third parties to include malicious tracking code or adware
Browser extensions permanently disable DNS lookups
Having more than two extensions causes operating systems to crash
Extensions automatically delete browsing history
explanation: Third-party extensions possess broad permissions to read web page DOMs, capture keystrokes, and inject scripts if their developers are bought out or compromised.

question: What is the primary objective of modern ransomware attacks?
options: To optimize database query execution speeds
To encrypt victim files and exfiltrate confidential data to extort financial ransom under threat of loss or leak
To overclock the victim's hardware graphics card
To fix operating system registry errors
explanation: Modern double-extortion ransomware denies operational access via encryption and threatens public leak of exfiltrated proprietary data.

question: If you notice your computer files are rapidly being renamed to strange extensions and a ransom note appears, what is the FIRST critical step?
options: Immediately disconnect the device from network (unplug Ethernet / disable Wi-Fi) and alert the SOC
Pay the ransom using personal funds immediately
Reboot the machine 5 times in a row
Copy the ransom note and email it to your friends
explanation: Network disconnection halts ransomware communication with C2 servers and prevents lateral movement/encryption across mapped network shares.

question: Which backup strategy provides the highest resilience against total ransomware destruction?
options: Saving a duplicate copy on the same local C:\ drive
The 3-2-1 backup rule: 3 copies of data, across 2 different media types, with at least 1 copy stored offline / air-gapped / immutable
Leaving an unencrypted USB hard drive plugged into the server 24/7
Relying solely on browser cache
explanation: Offline, immutable, or air-gapped backups cannot be reached or encrypted by ransomware executing inside the corporate network.

question: Which of the following would be classified as Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
options: Full Name, Social Security Number, Date of Birth, and Home Address
The official stock ticker symbol of a public company
The current temperature in London
The brand name of an enterprise router
explanation: PII is any data that can directly or indirectly identify, contact, or locate an individual, necessitating strict handling under privacy laws.

question: You need to send an internal financial report containing client bank details to an external auditor. What is the proper procedure?
options: Attach it as a plain unencrypted Excel spreadsheet over standard email
Use an enterprise-approved encrypted file transfer solution with recipient access controls
Post it in a public online forum and send the auditor a link
Upload it to a free public document converter tool on the web
explanation: Confidential financial data must be encrypted in transit and at rest, using authenticated and audited enterprise channels.

question: When working from a coffee shop or airport on public Wi-Fi, what security control should always be engaged before logging into business accounts?
options: An enterprise Virtual Private Network (VPN)
Enabling public file and printer sharing
Disabling your local endpoint firewall
Turning off browser pop-up blockers
explanation: A VPN encapsulates and encrypts your network traffic through a secure tunnel, protecting it from eavesdroppers on the untrusted local Wi-Fi.

question: What is an 'Evil Twin' Wi-Fi access point?
options: A rogue wireless access point configured with the same SSID as a legitimate public network to snoop on connected victims
A dual-band router operating at 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz
A device with two network interface cards
A backup router that turns on during power outages
explanation: An Evil Twin mimics a known SSID (like 'Airport_Free_WiFi') to trick devices into connecting, allowing the attacker to intercept traffic.

question: A newly installed mobile calculator app requests permissions to access your Contacts, Microphone, SMS messages, and GPS location. What should you do?
options: Grant all permissions because the developer probably needs them for math features
Deny excessive permissions and uninstall the application immediately
Leave your phone in airplane mode forever
Root / Jailbreak your device to bypass the prompt
explanation: Utility apps requesting intrusive permissions unrelated to core functionality often contain spyware, adware, or data scrapers.

question: Why does 'Jailbreaking' or 'Rooting' a mobile device pose a significant security threat to corporate data?
options: It disables built-in operating system sandboxing, code signing, and security exploit protections
It decreases the resolution of the screen
It prevents the device from connecting to 5G cellular networks
It makes the device battery charge too fast
explanation: Rooting bypasses OS security boundaries, allowing any rogue app with root access to inspect memory, steal tokens, and bypass device encryption.

question: You realize you accidentally entered your corporate password on a suspicious web page 10 minutes ago. What is the best immediate response?
options: Keep quiet and hope nobody notices so you do not get in trouble
Immediately report the mistake to IT Security / SOC and reset your password on a secure machine
Wait 7 days to see if suspicious activity happens before reporting
Delete your email inbox and shutdown the computer
explanation: Transparent, fast reporting is vital. Immediate notification allows the SOC to revoke active session tokens and block the attacker before deeper penetration occurs.

question: What is 'Dwell Time' in cybersecurity incident response?
options: The duration an analyst takes to brew coffee
The duration an attacker remains undetected inside a victim's network before discovery
The time it takes for a hard drive to format
The time an employee spends on annual awareness training
explanation: Dwell time measures the elapsed time from initial unauthorized breach to detection. Reducing dwell time is a primary objective of threat intelligence and SOC monitoring.

question: Why is installing security updates ('patches') promptly critical for maintaining defensive posture?
options: Patches repair known vulnerabilities that threat actors actively weaponize into automated exploits
Patches increase internet bandwidth speeds
Patches remove all previous files from the system
Patches change the desktop wallpaper each month
explanation: When vendors publish CVE patches, adversaries reverse-engineer the fixes to craft exploits targeting organizations that delay patch deployment.

question: You find a brand-new 128GB USB flash drive sitting on the sidewalk outside your office building labeled 'CONFIDENTIAL_PAYROLL_2026.xlsx'. What should you do?
options: Plug it into your workstation to see whose payroll it is
Format it on your company laptop so you can reuse the free storage
Do NOT plug it in; hand it directly to Physical Security or the SOC as potential USB baiting
Take it home and plug it into your personal gaming PC
explanation: USB baiting drops weaponized drives configured with BadUSB microcontrollers that execute automated keystroke injection payloads when connected.

question: An employee receives a voice call from someone who sounds identical to their direct supervisor asking for an emergency wire transfer to an unknown vendor. How should the employee handle this?
options: Execute the transfer immediately since the voice sounded familiar
Validate the request through established secondary communication channels or pre-arranged authorization protocols before executing any transaction
Ignore company wire policies because executive requests always override procedures
Post about the call on public social media
explanation: Generative AI voice cloning tools can replicate an individual's vocal timbre from short public audio clips. Dual-control out-of-band verification prevents deepfake fraud.

question: What is the primary risk of using personal information (e.g. pet names, high school name, children's birth years) in passwords?
options: These details are often publicly discoverable through social media reconnaissance (OSINT) and easily cracked via dictionary attacks
They cause keyboard keys to wear out faster
They are blocked by the international Unicode consortium
They automatically disable firewall rules
explanation: OSINT reconnaissance allows attackers to build custom wordlists targeting specific victims with personal biographical data.

question: What is a 'Drive-By Download'?
options: Downloading files while driving a motor vehicle
An unintended download of malicious software that occurs automatically without the user's explicit consent simply by visiting a compromised webpage
Downloading software over a satellite link
A fast file transfer protocol used in SOCs
explanation: Drive-by downloads leverage browser or plugin vulnerabilities to install malicious payloads silently in the background when visiting a compromised site.

question: Why is SMS-based verification generally considered less secure than hardware security keys or authenticator apps?
options: SMS text messages are vulnerable to SIM swapping, SS7 signaling interception, and network eavesdropping
SMS requires an active Wi-Fi connection at all times
SMS messages cannot display numbers greater than 999
SMS is incompatible with modern smartphones
explanation: Adversaries can bribe or trick mobile carriers into transferring a victim's phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM card (SIM swapping), capturing all incoming SMS 2FA codes.
